In re : Cran 2 of 2025
1.

The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that there are ample evidence that the present petitioner was a juvenile at the time of commission of the offence and that has been enquired into by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Sealdah and, accordingly, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Sealdah has recorded an order dated September 12,
2025, wherein he observed, inter alia, as follows :
"When this court held another enquiry in terms of the kind direction of the Hon'ble Court it also appears that on the date of incident this convict/appellant was a C.C.L.
as per provision of section 2(13) of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children), Act, 2015.
In order to reach to the said conclusion, I have relied upon the transfer certificate dated 06.01.2014 issued by TIC Sarwodaya Vidyalaya.

2. It also appears from the record that on March 3, 2019, a case under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the POCSO Act was initiated at Ultadanga Police Station on the basis of a complaint of the victim's father.
After investigation, the Investigating Agency has submitted chargesheet being Charge Sheet No.31 of 2019 dated March 18, 2019.

After trial the sole accused Akshay Kumar Singh was found guilty and he was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for twenty years and to pay a fine of rupees two lacs for offence under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.

3. At present, the learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that by virtue of the order dated September 12, 2025, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Sealdah has come to a conclusion that at the time of alleged commission of offence, the present petitioner was a juvenile.

4. The learned counsel for the State has also submitted that the petitioner was a juvenile at the time of commission of the offence, as per report of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court,
Sealdah.
5. The learned counsel for the de facto complainant is also present in Court.
6. In view of such findings of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Sealdah, we are inclined to allow the prayer for bail of the petitioner.

7. It is thus ORDERED that the applicant/appellant, namely, Akshay Kumar Singh shall be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) to the satisfaction of the Learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Sealdah, South 24-Parganas cum Special Judge (under POCSO Act), Sealdah subject to the condition that the petitioner shall not leave the district Kolkata except for the purpose of attending court proceedings till disposal of the appeal.

8.

The department is directed to forward a copy of this order to the Superintendent of the concerned Correctional Home for immediate release of the applicant/appellant unless he is wanted in connection with any other case.

9. We clarify that the observations made by us in this order are only for the purpose of disposing of the application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no relevance at the final hearing of the appeal.
10. The application being I.A. No. CRAN 2 of 2025 is, accordingly, disposed of.
